questions.stem: The word 'PHILANTHROPY' contains the roots 'phil' (love) and 'anthrop' (human). What does PHILANTHROPY mean?

options.option_text: Love of mankind; charitable goodwill towards others

questions.explanation: C is correct. PHILANTHROPY = phil (love) + anthrop (human/mankind) = love of humanity; active charitable effort to promote human welfare. PHILANTHROPIST = one who practices philanthropy. Related: misanthropy (hatred of people), anthropology (study of humans), philosophy (love of wisdom).

questions.stem: Which word contains the root 'CHRON' meaning 'time'?
questions.explanation: A is correct. CHRON = time (Greek). Words with 'chron': chronicle (time-ordered account), chronological (arranged in time order), synchronise (together+time = occur at same time), anachronism (out of time/era), chronometer (time-measuring instrument), chronic (lasting a long time).

questions.stem: The root 'RUPT' means 'to break'. Which word means 'impossible to break or corrupt'?
questions.explanation: C is correct. RUPT = break (Latin rumpere). INCORRUPTIBLE = in (not) + corr (thoroughly) + rupt (break) = cannot be broken/corrupted. Family: interrupt (break between), erupt (break out), disrupt (break apart), bankrupt (bench+break = broken businessman), abrupt (broken off suddenly).

questions.stem: The prefix 'AMBI-' or 'AMPHI-' means 'both' or 'on both sides'. Which word means 'able to use both hands equally well'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. AMBIDEXTROUS = ambi (both) + dexter (right hand in Latin = skilled) = skilled on both sides = able to use both hands with equal ease. AMBI- words: ambiguous (both+driven = two meanings), ambivalent (both+value = conflicting feelings), ambidextrous (both+dexterous). AMPHI- words: amphibian (both+life = lives in water and land), amphitheatre (both+theatre = open-air stage).

questions.stem: The root 'MNEMONIC' comes from the Greek 'mneme' meaning 'memory'. A MNEMONIC is:

options.option_text: A device or pattern that aids memory recall
The inability to form new memories

questions.explanation: B is correct. MNEMONIC = a memory aid (acronym, rhyme, or pattern). Example: 'VIBGYOR' for rainbow colours. Root: Greek mneme (memory). Related words: amnesia (a=without + mnesia = loss of memory), amnesty (a+mnesty = forgetting offences = pardon), Mnemosyne (Greek goddess of memory).

questions.stem: Which of the following contains the Latin root 'VID/VIS' meaning 'to see'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. VID/VIS = see (Latin videre). EVIDENCE = e (out) + vid (see) = what is observed, proof. Other VIS/VID words: visible (able to be seen), vision (sight), television (tele+vision = far+see), evident (clearly seen), supervise (super+vis = oversee), provision (pro+vis = see ahead), video (I see).

questions.stem: The suffix '-CRACY' comes from the Greek 'kratos' meaning 'rule/power'. What does 'PLUTOCRACY' mean?
questions.explanation: C is correct. PLUTOCRACY = ploutos (wealth) + kratos (power/rule) = government by the wealthy. -CRACY words: democracy (demos=people), aristocracy (aristos=best), oligarchy (oligos=few), theocracy (theos=god), bureaucracy (bureau=office), plutocracy (ploutos=wealth), meritocracy (merit=worth).

questions.stem: The prefix 'PSEUDO-' means 'false'. Which of the following means 'a false name used by an author'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. PSEUDONYM = pseudo (false) + nym/onym (name) = a pen name or alias used by an author. Example: Samuel Clemens used the pseudonym 'Mark Twain'. -onym words: synonym (same+name), antonym (opposite+name), acronym (acro+name = initial letters), homonym (same name, different meaning).

questions.stem: The root 'PORT' means 'to carry'. Which word means 'to carry back goods to one's home country'?
questions.explanation: C is correct. IMPORT = im (in) + port (carry) = carry into one's country. PORT words: export (carry out), import (carry in), transport (carry across), portable (capable of being carried), porter (one who carries), deport (carry away from a country), support (carry from below = sustain).

questions.stem: The Latin root 'OMNI' means 'all'. Which word means 'eating all kinds of food — both plants and animals'?
questions.explanation: C is correct. OMNIVOROUS = omni (all) + vorous (eating) = eating all types of food. Humans are omnivores. OMNI- words: omniscient (omni+scient=all+knowing = all-knowing), omnipotent (omni+potent=all+powerful = all-powerful), omnipresent (all+present = existing everywhere), omnivorous (all+eating).

questions.stem: The prefix 'BENE-' means 'good/well'. Which word means 'a gift or donation to a good cause'?
questions.explanation: C is correct. BENEFACTION = bene (well/good) + factio (doing) = a charitable act or donation. BENEFACTOR = one who gives a benefaction. BENE- words: benefit (well+fitted = advantage), benevolent (well+wishing), beneficiary (one who receives benefit), benediction (well+speak = blessing). MALE-/MALE- is the opposite: malevolent (ill+wishing), malefactor (evil-doer).
